Overview

Source: vignettes/overview.Rmd
overview.Rmd

Original MUI X documentation: Tree View - Overview and Quickstart. The examples of this documentation are written for R.

muiTreeView gives access to MUI X Tree View React components, which let users navigate hierarchical lists of data with nested levels that can be expanded and collapsed. It works in Shiny apps, Quarto documents, R Markdown and in static HTML pages.

Install 

install.packages("muiTreeView")
# or the development version
remotes::install_github("lgnbhl/muiTreeView")
library(muiTreeView)

Community version only

MUI X Tree View ships in two packages: the free Community version (@mui/x-tree-view, MIT license) and the commercial Pro version (@mui/x-tree-view-pro). muiTreeView wraps the Community version only, so the Pro features (virtualization, lazy loading, drag and drop ordering) are not available. MUI docs

Simple Tree View or Rich Tree View?

The Tree View comes as two components:

  • SimpleTreeView() takes its items as TreeItem() children. It is the natural choice for navigation, such as a sidebar or a file explorer, where you write each item by hand and can put any UI in its label.
  • RichTreeView() takes its items as data, through the items argument. It is the natural choice for exploring a dataset: build the items from a data frame with asMuiTree().

Rich Tree View from a data frame

asMuiTree() turns the columns of a data frame into the levels of the tree. Here, a selection of the functions of three companion packages, muiMaterial, muiCharts and reactRouter, grouped by package and topic:

fns <- rbind(
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Layout", fn = c("Box", "Stack", "Grid")),
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Inputs", fn = c("Button", "TextField", "Slider", "Switch")),
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Navigation", fn = c("Link", "Tabs", "Drawer")),
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Surfaces", fn = c("AppBar", "Toolbar", "Card")),
  data.frame(package = "muiCharts", group = "Charts", fn = c("BarChart", "LineChart", "PieChart", "Gauge")),
  data.frame(package = "muiCharts", group = "Building blocks", fn = c("ChartsContainer", "ChartsXAxis", "ChartsLegend", "Toolbar")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Routers", fn = c("RouterProvider", "createHashRouter", "createMemoryRouter")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Routes", fn = c("Route", "Outlet")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Navigation", fn = c("Link", "NavLink", "Navigate")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Hooks", fn = c("useParams", "useLoaderData", "useNavigate"))
)
head(fns)
#>       package  group        fn
#> 1 muiMaterial Layout       Box
#> 2 muiMaterial Layout     Stack
#> 3 muiMaterial Layout      Grid
#> 4 muiMaterial Inputs    Button
#> 5 muiMaterial Inputs TextField
#> 6 muiMaterial Inputs    Slider

RichTreeView(
  items = asMuiTree(fns)
)

See Data frames with asMuiTree() for stable ids, extra fields and tibbles. MUI docs

Simple Tree View for navigation 

SimpleTreeView(
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiMaterial"),
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "muiMaterial",
    label = "muiMaterial",
    TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::Button", label = "Button()"),
    TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::TextField", label = "TextField()"),
    TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::Drawer", label = "Drawer()")
  ),
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "muiCharts",
    label = "muiCharts",
    TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::BarChart", label = "BarChart()"),
    TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::LineChart", label = "LineChart()")
  ),
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "reactRouter",
    label = "reactRouter",
    TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::RouterProvider", label = "RouterProvider()"),
    TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::Route", label = "Route()"),
    TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::NavLink", label = "NavLink()")
  )
)

Main features 

RichTreeView(
  items = asMuiTree(fns),
  checkboxSelection = TRUE,
  multiSelect = TRUE
)
Feature Simple Tree View Rich Tree View
Items Items Items
Selection Selection Selection
Expansion Expansion Expansion
Customization Customization Customization
Label editing – Label editing

The Tree Item customization and Accessibility pages apply to both components.

In an app

  • Shiny: send the selection, expansion and clicks to the server with setInput().
  • reactRouter: use a tree view as the navigation of a multi-page app, without a Shiny server.
  • Theming: use a muiMaterial theme, dark mode, and avoid Bootstrap conflicts.

Every exported function also has a runnable Shiny example:

list.files(system.file("examples", package = "muiTreeView"))
source(system.file("examples/RichTreeView.R", package = "muiTreeView"))

Use other MUI products

MUI X Tree View is developed by MUI, the company behind the popular React framework Material UI. muiTreeView is a companion to the R package muiMaterial, which provides access to all Material UI components from R.
